## Observation
Split from d23c. On the Windows sweep (run 35551741150, job 106187634058, 2026-09-21) op-cert tests fail because `rebar.attest.sshsig.ssh_keygen_version()` finds no usable OpenSSH, and signing needs 8.9 or newer. Reproduced on this macOS host (real ssh is OpenSSH 10.3 and passes all 97 tests below) with a PATH shim whose `ssh -V` prints `OpenSSH_8.8p1`: 50 of 97 tests in 5 modules fail. 46 of those 50 also fail in the Windows log with an OpenSSH-related message.

| module | tests | fail under shim |
|---|---:|---:|
| tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py | 12 | 11 |
| tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py | 39 | 15 |
| tests/unit/test_opcert_binding_thread_propagation_ff4a.py | 8 | 5 |
| tests/unit/test_opcert_producer_seam_8d8e.py | 24 | 17 |
| tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py | 14 | 2 |

## Suspected cause (partly checked)
The probe's regex is `OpenSSH_(\d+)\.(\d+)`. Checked here: it returns `None` for the strings `OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p1, LibreSSL 3.8.2` and `OpenSSH_for_Windows_8.1p1, LibreSSL 3.0.2`, and parses `OpenSSH_9.5p1` and `OpenSSH_8.8p1`. NOT checked: the banner the runner's `ssh -V` really prints, and whether the `windows-2025-vs2026` image has OpenSSH at all (the plain `windows-2025` readme lists none, and the job log has no `ssh -V` output). If the runner has no OpenSSH, this fix changes nothing there and d23c's skip is the effective guard.

## Decision (user, 2026-10-25)
Fix the version probe to parse the `OpenSSH_for_Windows_<ver>` form, failing test first. Keep d23c's per-test skip as the fallback. Skipping the other 45 tests individually was not chosen.

## Plan
1. New module `tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig_version_banner.py` (the existing sshsig modules skip when ssh-keygen is absent, so they cannot hold it). It mocks `subprocess.run` inside `rebar.attest.sshsig` and parametrizes `ssh_keygen_version()` over banners: `OpenSSH_9.5p1, OpenSSL 3.0.2` -> (9, 5); `OpenSSH_8.8p1, OpenSSL 3.0.2` -> (8, 8); `OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p1, LibreSSL 3.8.2` -> (9, 5); `OpenSSH_for_Windows_8.1p1, LibreSSL 3.0.2` -> (8, 1); a banner on stdout instead of stderr; unparseable text -> None; `FileNotFoundError` -> None. Also `ensure_available()` raises for the Windows 8.1 banner and not for the Windows 9.5 banner. Run it first: the two Windows-form cases that expect a version must fail on the current code.
2. In `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`, change `_VERSION_RE` to `OpenSSH_(?:for_Windows_)?(\d+)\.(\d+)`. Nothing else in the file changes.

Out of scope: probing `ssh-keygen` instead of `ssh`, provisioning OpenSSH on the runner, and the Windows file-permission question in 47d8-baf8-2348-45c9.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The new banner tests fail on the current code for the two `OpenSSH_for_Windows_` cases that expect a version and pass after the change (checked: both `pytest tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig_version_banner.py -q` runs recorded in a ticket comment).
- [x] With a PATH shim whose `ssh -V` prints `OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p1, LibreSSL 3.8.2`, the 5 modules above report 50 failed before the change and 0 failed after, and with this host's real ssh they report 97 passed both times (checked: the four `pytest` summaries recorded in a ticket comment).
- [x] Only `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py` and the new test module change (checked: `git diff --stat origin/main` lists exactly those two files).
- [x] `make verify` shows no failure outside the known pandoc set, and the Gerrit change is `Verified +1`.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig_version_banner.py tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig.py tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig_heldout.py -q
make verify
```
